name: Material 3 (Compose)
description: Material Design 3 (baseline, light and dark theme) for Jetpack Compose, with each type's composable in `code`. The symbols and parameters come from the androidx code at compose.material3 version 1.4.0 (commit 5113b82a4ed6416d6344efa50e41db8cb65928ff). Conventions: the slots (lambdas) of each composable are described in `notes`; size comes from width, height and weight; icons are Icons.Filled suggestions (the ones androidx puts in Icons.AutoMirrored flip in rtl); the reading direction and the anchor draw the tooltip (with its arrow), the badge and the menu anchored; the remote image uses the app's image loader; the Scaffold places each child in the right slot by its type.

annotationTypes.name: Scaffold

fields.description: Preferred color for the content inside the scaffold. Empty = the Material 3 default.

compose.notes: Each child marking goes in the argument of its slot, chosen by the type and then by the geometry: `top-app-bar` (or `search-bar`) in `topBar`, `navigation-bar`, `short-navigation-bar` or `bottom-app-bar` in `bottomBar`, `fab` and `extended-fab` in `floatingActionButton`, `snackbar` in `snackbarHost` and the rest in `content = { innerPadding -> … }`, applying `Modifier.padding(innerPadding)` to the first child of the content. A `modal` `bottom-sheet` goes in the content (the `ModalBottomSheet` opens over the screen); the `standard` one is the `BottomSheetScaffold` itself and replaces the Scaffold. With width and height `fill`, use `Modifier.fillMaxSize()`; `snackbarHost` (with no `snackbar` child) and `contentWindowInsets` stay at their defaults.

Width and position come from the `Modifier` (the row has no size of its own; it usually goes under the `TopAppBar` or above the page content). Since material3 1.4.0 icons require `androidx.compose.material:material-icons-core` (or `-extended`) or a Material Symbol downloaded with `painterResource`; the ones that mirror (ArrowBack, KeyboardArrowRight, List) live in `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled`. `iconDescription` names an icon-only row (no `label`), and is `null` when the row has a `label` that already names it.

compose.notes: Stable overload `BottomAppBar(actions = { … }, floatingActionButton = { … })`, without `scrollBehavior` (the overload with `scrollBehavior` requires `@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)` and is not used here). Each filled `actionIcon1` to `actionIcon4` becomes an `IconButton(onClick = …) { Icon(Icons.Filled.<actionIconN>, contentDescription = <actionIconNDescription>) }` inside `actions = { … }` (a `RowScope`, from left to right). With `floatingActionButton` filled, `floatingActionButton = { FloatingActionButton(onClick = …, containerColor = BottomAppBarDefaults.bottomAppBarFabColor, elevation = FloatingActionButtonDefaults.bottomAppBarFabElevation()) { Icon(Icons.Filled.<floatingActionButton>, contentDescription = <floatingActionButtonDescription>) } }`; empty = omit the parameter. Inside a Scaffold, the bar goes in `bottomBar`. The height (80, plus the system navigation bar) belongs to the component: width and position come from the `Modifier`. Since material3 1.4.0 icons require `androidx.compose.material:material-icons-core` (or `-extended`) or a Material Symbol downloaded with `painterResource`; the ones that mirror (ArrowBack, KeyboardArrowRight, List) live in `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled`. With child markings in the `actions` slot the node carries `actions = { … }` with an `IconButton` (or the child's own call) for each one, and the `actionIcon1` to `actionIcon4` of `values` are the default content that the children replace (they are not arguments then); with a child in the `floatingActionButton` slot the node carries `floatingActionButton = { … }` with it and the `floatingActionButton` field's icon is not used. Without child markings the arguments are the ones above. The accessible names are fields (`actionIcon1Description`, `actionIcon2Description`, `actionIcon3Description`, `actionIcon4Description` and `floatingActionButtonDescription`): they go in the `contentDescription` of the `Icon` and are not arguments of the bar (`get_code_hints` hands them over in `accessibility.parts`). A child in a slot answers for its own label.

fields.label: Maximum small item width (dp)
fields.description: Maximum allowed width of the small items, in dp. The small item's width is chosen between `minSmallItemWidth` and `maxSmallItemWidth`, according to `preferredItemWidth` and the carousel width.

fields.label: Vertical (dp)

compose.notes: Requires @OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class) (the three carousels, the `CarouselState` and the `CarouselItemScope` are experimental at the pinned commit). `state = rememberCarouselState { <number of rows of items> }` (the `itemCount` is the trailing lambda) and `content = { index -> … }` draws the item `items[index]`, inside the `CarouselItemScope`: a remote image with the app's loader (for example Coil `AsyncImage(model = <image>, contentDescription = <label>, contentScale = ContentScale.Crop, modifier = Modifier.height(205.dp).maskClip(MaterialTheme.shapes.extraLarge))`, outside androidx); `maskClip` belongs to the item's scope and gives the clip that follows the scroll; a filled `label` becomes a `Text(<label>)` over the image, in a `Box`. The item width is a required parameter depending on the style: `preferredItemWidth = <preferredItemWidth>.dp` in multi-browse and `itemWidth = <itemWidth>.dp` in uncontained; centered-hero takes no width (the optional `maxItemWidth` is not mapped). `itemSpacing` becomes `<itemSpacing>.dp`. The height comes from the item (`Modifier.height(…)`), not from the carousel. Size: `fill` becomes `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`/`fillMaxHeight()`, `fixed` becomes `Modifier.width(<marking width>.dp)`/`height(<marking height>.dp)` and `weight` becomes `Modifier.weight(<weight>f)` (only inside Row, Column or FlowRow).

compose.notes: Stable, no opt-in. `isRefreshing` connects to a screen state (`var isRefreshing by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`) and `onRefresh = { /* starts the refresh and sets isRefreshing to true; when done, back to false */ }`. The `indicator` and the `state` (`rememberPullToRefreshState()`) stay at their defaults: the 40 dp circular indicator at the top. `contentAlignment` is the Box's own. Size: `fill` becomes `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`/`fillMaxHeight()`, `fixed` becomes `Modifier.width(<marking width>.dp)`/`height(<marking height>.dp)` and `weight` becomes `Modifier.weight(<weight>f)` (only inside Row, Column or FlowRow).

annotationTypes.name: SwipeToDismissBox
annotationTypes.description: Item that is dismissed by swiping to one side or the other, revealing a background with an icon (delete, archive). Use in list items.

fields.description: Main line of the dismissible item (the content belongs to the app; the drawing shows a list item).

fields.label: Supporting text
fields.description: Supporting line below the title. Empty = no line.

fields.label: Swipe state
fields.description: Settled is the item at rest; StartToEnd and EndToStart show the swiped item and the revealed background (SwipeToDismissBoxValue).

fields.description: false prevents swiping in the reading direction (enableDismissFromStartToEnd).

fields.label: Dismiss from end to start
fields.description: false prevents swiping against the reading direction (enableDismissFromEndToStart).

fields.label: Background icon
fields.description: Icon of the revealed background (the drawing shows Delete, Done, Check, Favorite, Edit, Star, Share, Add and Close; others fall back to Delete). Empty = Delete.

fields.label: Background icon description
fields.description: Accessible description of the background icon, read by a screen reader. Empty = the icon is decorative and is not announced.

fields.label: Width
fields.description: wrap fits the content, fill takes all the available width and fixed uses the marking's width (dp).

fields.label: Height
fields.description: wrap fits the content, fill takes all the available height and fixed uses the marking's height (dp).

fields.label: Weight

fields.label: Gestures enabled
fields.description: Defines whether swipe-to-dismiss can be operated by gestures.

compose.notes: Stable, no opt-in. Use the overload with `onDismiss` (the one that only takes `content` and `backgroundContent` and reads `state.currentValue` is `@Deprecated`). `state = rememberSwipeToDismissBoxState(initialValue = <direction>)`: the `direction` field is the state's `initialValue` (it is not a parameter of `SwipeToDismissBox`) and, in general, stays at `Settled`; the two `enableDismiss…` are parameters of the box. `onDismiss = { value -> … }` removes the item (the app handles `StartToEnd` and `EndToStart`). `backgroundContent` (a `RowScope`) is the revealed background: a `Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize().background(<color>).padding(horizontal = 24.dp), contentAlignment = if (state.dismissDirection == SwipeToDismissBoxValue.StartToEnd) Alignment.CenterStart else Alignment.CenterEnd) { Icon(Icons.Filled.<icon>, contentDescription = <iconDescription>) }`; the background colors belong to the app. The `content` (a `RowScope`) is the item, usually a `ListItem` or `Card` (the child marking, or whatever the app already has). Size: `fill` becomes `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()`/`fillMaxHeight()`, `fixed` becomes `Modifier.width(<marking width>.dp)`/`height(<marking height>.dp)` and `weight` becomes `Modifier.weight(<weight>f)` (only inside Row, Column or FlowRow). `iconDescription` is empty (`null`) when the icon is decorative.
